profile.reading: Petadata occupies a single suite, number 116, at 39159 Paseo Padre Parkway in Fremont, within Alameda County's stretch of the San Francisco Bay Area technology corridor. The OpenStreetMap record tags the site as a data center, and the name itself, a play on petabyte, points toward a company built around large scale data storage or hosting. A suite number at a multi tenant business address is a common way small IT, colocation, or managed hosting firms lease space rather than own a purpose built building, so a modest storage or backup operation at this location is plausible. It would not be a hyperscale campus. No operating company website could be confirmed at this address. The dot com domain sharing the Petadata name is a resale listing unconnected to any data business, and no working site could be reached at the more likely petadata dot io address. Without a confirmed operator site, business registration, or press coverage tied to this suite, its exact function, whether that is a small hosting company, IT services office, or another kind of tenant entirely, cannot be established from public information. This entry is published as an honest placeholder rather than a guess, and will be updated if a confirmed operator surfaces.

reading.body:
Petadata is an unresolved entry, not a confirmed AI data center, and no power, cooling, or IT load figures exist for it.

The record places a single leased suite, number 116, at 39159 Paseo Padre Parkway in Fremont, tagged as a data center on OpenStreetMap. A suite inside a multi-tenant business address is the shape of a small hosting, colocation, or IT tenant, not a purpose-built facility. The name echoes petabyte, but the name is the only evidence of what the business does. No operator website, business registration, or press coverage could be confirmed, and the two domains sharing the name resolve to an unrelated resale listing and a dead address.

For AI infrastructure the relevant fact is the absence of numbers. Compute buildout is measured in megawatts of load and cooling capacity, and this site publishes none. California carries 103 mapped facilities, of which 11 have published capacity totaling 365 MW. Petadata cannot be placed in that ranking, and its zero megawatts in the data is a missing measurement rather than a measured zero.

What this does not tell the reader is whether a data business operates here at all. It may be a small storage or backup tenant, an IT office, or a mistagged unrelated business. The coordinates and address are confirmed. Everything past the address is not.
